label: early copy phase, a v is about to be output
explanation: Fires almost only in the copy phase (99.9% of activation mass). It is silent in the original phase and at <DEL>. It is strongest at the first copy steps: recall_idx 1 holds 60% of mass, the step right after <DEL> has lift 6x, and recall_idx 1-3 hold about 95%. Whether and how strongly it fires depends on which tokens are coming up in the output, above all v. When v is output now or next, the rate is about 35-40% (lift 10-11x), and the top activations (up to 6.7) are all sequences like o v v v m that open with v runs, with activation peaking at the step that outputs the token right before the vs. u, w, i and s raise the rate less. Without an upcoming v it fires weakly and diffusely across early copy steps. Rate falls as the number of digits in the sequence goes up. The predicate (recall_idx <= 3 and v output within the next 3 steps) gets about 0.64 precision and 0.45 recall on dev. Widening it to the {v,u,w,i} set raises mass recall to 0.86 but cuts precision to 0.35. Many weak activations are left unexplained.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the next token to output (most: v, u, i, s, w, d; least: f, z, r, 0) and the token being output (most: v, u, w, i, s, t; least: 0, p, z, f); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, phase=2, t=7.
